solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Took soft toy as prize as usual (6)

blocks.note: to win is to take something as a prize
a ted is a teddy bear

annotation.surface: A child walks off with a cuddly toy as a prize, as happens every time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As prize' tells you which sense of 'took' is meant: WON, not stole or grabbed.
annotation.definitionFit: Wonted means customary or usual, as in 'with her wonted calm'.

entries.clue: Egg with no alcohol in mixed-up state (8)

annotation.definition: Egg with no alcohol in mixed-up state

indicators.note: 'in' means inside, so the teetotal TT is placed inside the MELEE

blocks.note: an egg is O-shaped, as in a duck's egg for a zero score
a melee is a confused scramble

annotation.surface: A cook beats an egg into a mess without adding any booze.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the dish: an omelette is egg mixed up, with no alcohol needed.
annotation.definitionFit: An omelette is beaten egg cooked in a pan: an egg mixed up, with nothing stronger added.

entries.clue: They’re regularly lacking finish (8)

indicators.note: at regular intervals, so take every other letter

annotation.surface: Some people routinely fail to see things through.
annotation.walkthrough: 'They’re' looks like the subject of a sentence; it is only letter fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a terminus is the end of the line, where a journey finishes.

entries.clue: Attractive, but at risk of being stripped of knighthood? (9)

annotation.definition2: at risk of being stripped of knighthood

blocks.clueFragment: at risk of being stripped of knighthood
blocks.note: a cryptic reading: DE- means removing, SIR is a knight's title, and -ABLE means liable to

annotation.surface: A handsome knight worries he might lose his title.
annotation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word into DE (removing), SIR (a knight's title) and ABLE: fit to have one's knighthood taken away.
annotation.definitionFit: Desirable means worth wanting, attractive.

entries.clue: Vigorous, but not pound on piano? So inadequate (8)

indicators.note: 'not pound' means without the pound, so its letter L is taken out
in an across clue, placed after the piano's P

blocks.note: L = pound (libra); remove it from ATHLETIC to leave ATHETIC

annotation.surface: A pianist who plays gently rather than hammering the keys is judged feeble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pound on piano' paints someone thumping the keys; pound is L and piano is P.
annotation.definitionFit: Pathetic in its everyday sense means feeble or inadequate.

entries.clue: Reasonable to be under pressure to damage a business dealing with drugs (15)

indicators.note: in a down clue, LOGICAL sits below the rest

annotation.surface: Pressure on a drug firm to do harm is presented as reasonable.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue starts with the last piece: 'Reasonable' comes first but LOGICAL ends the answer because it sits under everything else.
annotation.definitionFit: Pharmacological means concerned with drugs and their effects.

entries.clue: Possessed article, having searched around (7)

indicators.note: HUNTED goes around the article

annotation.surface: Someone who owns an item has been rummaging about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Possessed' looks like 'owned'; here it means gripped by a spirit.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in its supernatural sense: gripped or occupied by a spirit.

entries.clue: Small computer at work on this? (8)

annotation.definition: Small computer at work on this?

blocks.note: a tablet is a small touchscreen computer

annotation.surface: Where might you put a tablet computer while working?
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a tabletop is where a small computer might sit while you work on it.
annotation.definitionFit: A tabletop is the flat surface on which you might rest a tablet.

entries.clue: Able to heal dog, indigenous breed, having removed lead (8)

indicators.note: the lead is the first letter, so drop N

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a native breed is an indigenous one

annotation.surface: A dog of a local breed, off its lead, turns out to have healing powers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a dog's leash; it is the leading letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Curative means having the power to cure, able to heal.

entries.clue: Understanding about getting underwear in a state (8)

indicators.note: 'about' means turned round, so KEN is read backwards
'getting' means receiving, so the reversed word takes in the underwear
'in' means inside, so the underwear sits inside the reversed word

annotation.surface: An agreement about underwear is reached while someone is in a state.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a state' reads as 'agitated'; 'in' is the container signal and 'state' is the US one.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of the fifty US states, in the Great Plains.

entries.clue: Burden powerless tradesman (6)

indicators.note: 'powerless' means with the power gone, so P, the symbol for power, is taken out

annotation.surface: A tradesman who has lost power is weighed down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Powerless' is one word in the clue but works as 'power' plus the deletion signal 'less'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as a verb: to saddle someone with an unwanted job.

entries.clue: Vape stuff on front of desk in small quantity (8)

indicators.note: in an across clue, ECIG RAM comes after the D
the front of a word is its beginning, so take its first letter

blocks.note: an e-cig is an electronic cigarette, a vape
to ram is to stuff or cram

annotation.surface: Someone puts a little vaping kit on the front of their desk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' reads as a noun, as in vaping gear; it is the verb RAM.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a tenth of a gram is a tiny weight.

entries.clue: Still a challenge to cross river (2,4)

indicators.note: A TEST goes across the river, containing it

annotation.surface: Crossing a river remains a challenge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' at the start reads as 'even now'; it means motionless.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: motionless, not stirring.

entries.clue: Not fancied or put forward? (8)

blocks.note: the straight sense: a horse nobody has bet on
the whimsical reading: undoing a move back means moving the other way, forward

annotation.surface: A horse no punter rates, or one never even entered.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put forward' looks like 'nominated'; the joke is that undoing 'backed' means moving forward.
annotation.definitionFit: Racing usage: a horse nobody has bet on is one the punters do not fancy.

entries.clue: Famous weapon without distinction we’re told (9)

indicators.note: what we are told we hear, so go by sound

blocks.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend

annotation.surface: A celebrated weapon is said to be unremarkable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Without distinction' reads as 'ordinary'; it is EX plus CALIBRE, which sounds like the end of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Excalibur is King Arthur's legendary sword.

entries.clue: Crack troops guarding European waters (4)

indicators.note: the troops surround the European

annotation.surface: Elite soldiers protect European territorial waters.
annotation.walkthrough: The SAS is the Special Air Service, the British Army's special forces regiment.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the salt waters covering most of the globe.

entries.clue: Napoleon’s rival succeeded at present social event (8)

annotation.surface: Napoleon's rival was a hit at a society gathering.
annotation.walkthrough: Not Wellington: in Orwell's Animal Farm, the pig Napoleon drives out his rival, the pig Snowball.
annotation.definitionFit: Snowball is the pig who challenges Napoleon in Animal Farm.

entries.clue: Longs to arrest evil hero (8)

indicators.note: ACHES holds ILL, as police hold a suspect

blocks.note: to ache for is to long for
ill as a noun means evil, harm

annotation.surface: Someone yearns to see a villainous hero arrested.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Evil hero' reads as one phrase; 'evil' is wordplay and 'hero' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Achilles is the Greek hero of the Trojan War.

entries.clue: Place in church programmes for audience (4)

indicators.note: an audience hears it, so go by sound

annotation.surface: Church services print programmes for the congregation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Programmes' suggests printed service sheets; it means software APPS.
annotation.definitionFit: The apse is the rounded recess at the east end of a church.

entries.clue: Fawns upon doctors delivering middle triplet (8)

indicators.note: handing over, so the middle three letters go

blocks.note: to doctor food or drink is to adulterate it
the middle three of eleven letters, TER, are removed

annotation.surface: Medics bringing a set of triplets into the world are fawned over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Doctors' reads as a noun, physicians; it is the verb meaning to tamper with.
annotation.definitionFit: To adulate is to flatter or fawn upon someone.

entries.clue: Colourist checks source of red filter (8)

indicators.note: holds back, so STAINER holds the R
the source of something is where it starts, so take the first letter

blocks.note: a stainer colours wood or cloth

annotation.surface: A painter inspects where the red pigment comes from.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Checks' reads as 'inspects'; it means restrains, holding the R inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a kitchen sieve that lets liquid through and holds solids back.

entries.clue: Dull epic novel is extremely clear (8)

indicators.note: new, so rearrange the letters

annotation.surface: A tedious long novel is perfectly easy to follow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Novel' sits by 'epic' and reads as a book; it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Pellucid means translucently clear, or very clear in meaning.

entries.clue: Fix what you and me mount for hero (7)

blocks.note: to peg is to fix in place
in dialect 'what' means 'as', as in 'the same what I did'

annotation.surface: Someone decides which horse the two of them will ride as heroes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mount' looks like a verb, to climb on; it is a noun, a steed.
annotation.definitionFit: Pegasus, the winged horse, was ridden by the hero Bellerophon.

entries.clue: Complaint with joint (6)

annotation.surface: A medical complaint affecting a joint.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complaint with joint' suggests arthritis; the complaint is a moan. A whinge is British slang for a grumble.
annotation.definitionFit: British informal: a peevish, moaning grumble.

entries.clue: Holding metal, back to front, turned to beat thin layer (4,4)

indicators.note: 'holding' means keeping inside, so the reversed beat contains the metal
the back letter of the metal moves round to its front
'turned' means turned round, so FLOG is read backwards

blocks.note: lead is a metal; moving its last letter to the front gives DLEA

annotation.surface: Metal, turned and beaten, becomes a thin film.
annotation.walkthrough: Fittingly, gold leaf is made by beating metal thin, but here the metal is LEAD and 'beat' is FLOG.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: precious metal hammered into a film used for gilding.

entries.clue: Most fit a book in case (6)

blocks.note: lest means in case, for fear that

annotation.surface: The healthiest people keep a book in its case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In case' looks like a container signal; it is the whole of LEST.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the most capable, fittest for a task.

entries.clue: Rank absence in court as a consequence (3,5)

indicators.note: 'in' means inside, so the absence sits inside the court

blocks.note: abs. is the abbreviation for absent in a register
'and' can mean 'and so', as in 'touch that and you'll be sorry'

annotation.surface: Failing to turn up in court has foul consequences.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like an adjective, foul; it is a taxi rank.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a taxi rank is where cabs wait in a row for fares.

entries.clue: Faust for one bewildered by sound of capital city (4,4)

indicators.note: use the sound, not the spelling

annotation.surface: Faust, confused by the din of a big city.
annotation.walkthrough: Faust sold his soul to the devil, so he is an example of a damned soul; 'for one' marks him as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Faust, having sold his soul to Mephistopheles, is the classic lost soul.

entries.clue: Series of prayers got up shortly with a line (6)

indicators.note: cut short, so ROSE loses its last letter

blocks.note: ROSE, got up, without its last letter

annotation.surface: Prayers are said after rising briefly and joining a queue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' reads as 'soon'; it trims the word before it.
annotation.definitionFit: The rosary is a set sequence of Catholic prayers counted on beads.
